# got

> `got` is a cross-platform Rust CLI and GitHub Action for shallow, sparse Git
> checkouts. It uses native Git, preserving normal commits and repository trees.

Use this file to orient AI agents and other language-model clients. For safe
automated workflows, read the agent guide before changing or pushing files.

## Core documentation

- [README](README.md): installation, requirements, and quick start.
- [Product requirements](PRD.md): scope, behavior, technical feasibility, and
  design decisions.
- [Agent usage guide](docs/agent-guide.md): safe CLI and Action workflows for
  coding agents.
- [Documentation-site llms.txt](docs/llms.txt): machine-readable links for the
  published documentation.
- [Repository agent instructions](AGENTS.md): contribution constraints and
  validation commands for agents working on this repository.
- [Documentation site source](docs/index.html): concise user-facing overview.
- [Cloudflare Worker configuration](wrangler.jsonc): deploy the static docs
  from `docs/` to `https://getgot.sh` with Cloudflare Workers Builds.

## Implementation

- [CLI source](src/main.rs): command parsing, checkout, Git pass-through, and
  push behavior.
- [Integration tests](tests/checkout.rs): local-remote checkout, commit, and
  push coverage.
- [GitHub Action metadata](action.yml): inputs, outputs, and execution setup.
- [GitHub Action script](action/checkout.sh): shallow sparse fetch and path
  validation.
- [Cross-platform CI](.github/workflows/ci.yml): Rust and Action checks on
  Ubuntu, macOS, and Windows.
- [Release workflow](.github/workflows/release.yml): builds platform archives
  and publishes GitHub Release assets.
- [Packaging instructions](packaging/README.md): supported install channels
  and release steps.
- [Linux installer](scripts/install-linux.sh): downloads and verifies the
  Linux x86_64 or ARM64 release archive.
- [Linux installer tests](tests/test_linux_installer.sh): exercises both
  supported architectures and rejects a tampered archive.

## Important behavior

- `got checkout <remote> [<path>]` requires a remote and creates a separate
  work branch at the latest tip of the remote's default branch unless another
  branch or reachable revision is selected. Omit the optional path for a full
  working tree, or supply a repository-relative path for a sparse checkout.
- Checkout is shallow; a supplied path enables sparse checkout. Blob filtering
  is used when supported; unsupported filtering produces a warning and keeps
  the checkout shallow.
- Cone-mode sparse checkout also materializes root files and parent-directory
  files required by Git. Commits remain ordinary full-repository commits.
- `got status`, `got add`, and `got commit` pass arguments to native Git.
- `got push` with arguments passes through to Git. Bare `got push` pushes the
  work branch, sets its upstream on first push, and warns if the recorded base
  branch advanced. It never rebases or force-pushes automatically and does not
  create a pull request.
- The Action accepts optional `path` and `additional-paths` inputs, defaults
  to depth 1, and checks out the full repository when neither path input is
  supplied. It exposes the resolved commit SHA and checkout directory as
  outputs.
- Release packages target macOS ARM64 via Homebrew
  (`brew install jimbobbennett/tap/got`), Windows x64/ARM64 via release ZIPs
  (WinGet is coming soon), and Linux x86_64/ARM64 via a checksum-verifying
  installer. Releases are built from version tags.
- The release workflow generates WinGet manifests, but the package will be
  available through WinGet after it is submitted and accepted. `cargo build`
  is used for release compilation, but Cargo is not an end-user installation
  channel.
